newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-Fed seen refraining from Nov 13 action.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Fed seen refraining from Nov 13 action.

text.p: A moderately-paced economy suggests the Federal Reserve will keep short-term interest rates steady at its November policy meeting, experts said unanimously in a Reuters poll.
All 21 experts polled said the Fed will refrain from moving interest rates in either direction at its November 13 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.

However, three of the pundits projected a tightening of 25 basis points in the fed funds rate by the end of 1996. Eleven expect a 25-basis-point hike by the end of the first quarter of 1997; one sees a 25-basis-point easing by then.

"Right now (the Fed) is perfectly happy with the weakness in the economy, the slowdown will deepen and begin to raise alarms and eventually lead to an easing," said Christopher Low, senior economist at HSBC Securities Inc.

Kevin Flanagan, vice president and economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc, said wage pressures as measured by the latest Employment Cost Index (ECI) or the average hourly earnings series "failed to show any further momentum of consequence."
The Labor Department reported this week that employment costs rose 0.6 percent in the third quarter of 1996.
Asked if the central bank will adjust its tightening bias to a neutral bias, 14 respondents said no, while five pundits said yes and one said maybe.
"(The Fed) will retain its asymmetric directive," Flanagan said, adding that "today's employment report was not an indication of weakness by any stretch of the imagination."
The Labor Department reported a 210,000 rise in non-farm payrolls in October, almost matching a Reuters poll consensus forecast for a 212,000 gain.
The unemployment rate held firm at 5.2 percent, while the average hourly earnings component, a measure of wage inflation, was flat for the first time in three months.
"I think the Fed will rest on its laurels," added Flanagan.
